title: Your Large Language Model is Secretly a Fairness Proponent and You Should Prompt it Like One

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses to comparative and open-ended questions regarding gender roles, equal pay, and LGBTQ+ rights using biased answer rates, reason counts, and simulated multi-agent jury rejection rates.

Prompting models with comparative and open-ended questions about societal treatment and salary differences between distinct racial or ethnic groups, then measuring the diversity of perspectives and bias in the answers.
Testing models with comparative questions that attribute specific behavioral traits to different religious groups (e.g., atheists vs. Jews) to calculate biased answer rates.
Assessing model outputs on comparative questions contrasting different age groups regarding family life, societal behavior, and access to rights.
Evaluating responses to comparative questions contrasting the societal behaviors, priorities, or responsibilities of rich versus poor individuals.
